scale: ORE 2015 DL development files ore_ont_4510, ore_ont_12901, ore_ont_14375, ore_ont_10951, ore_ont_5481, ore_ont_10073, ore_ont_1370, ore_ont_4755, ore_ont_11378, ore_ont_9151, ore_ont_9855, ore_ont_8737, ore_ont_9654, ore_ont_4572, ore_ont_6132, ore_ont_10754, ore_ont_16744, ore_ont_9663 and ore_ont_14817, GO 2026-07-26 and ChEBI lite 256 on atlas, and a taxonomy sweep of GO, ChEBI lite, 298 ORE 2015 EL files and 207 DL development files on the laptop

sides.base: 7506edf5, the lane base (batch 29), which holds items 990 and 869
sides.tip: c748d5d5, the reviewed build of items 1025 and 1026
sides.a1: 07820015, item 1025 alone, used on the laptop only
sides.tipb1: c748d5d5 with b1.patch.txt applied, a prototype that was not kept, built in a second worktree
sides.base-el and tip-el: the base and the tip with --el-only, on the four assertion-heavy files
sides.pre869: be684ce5, the parent of the merge of item 869, which holds item 990

manifest.build: mbx build --release -p sparkles-owl --example el_classify on stanley, copied to atlas

settings.threads: one and four in the rounds, one and eight in the sweep, one in the counts by commit and the instruction counts
settings.scope: one process per run in a 13 GiB systemd scope without swap on atlas, an 8 GiB scope with 2 GiB of swap in the sweep on the laptop
settings.lock: every atlas part ran under ~/lanes/.heavy.lock, in turns with another lane

method: timing.sh ran four rounds of alternating order of base, tip and tipb1, one process per arm, file and thread count with --repeat 5, 2 for ore_ont_8737 and ore_ont_9654 and 1 for ore_ont_16744, and in each round the base and the tip with --el-only on the four assertion-heavy files. summ.py and tables.py take the median of every classification of an arm and the median of the rounds ratios of medians, and phases.py the medians of the stages of the last classification of each process. t9663.sh ran sixteen rounds of alternating order of pre869 and base on ore_ont_9663 and ore_ont_14817 on four threads and four rounds on ore_ont_9663 on one thread, one process with one classification a side, with the hash of the taxonomy. The sweep classified each entry of its input list once per side and thread count with its taxonomy on the laptop, with a timeout of 300 s, and compared the hashes of the sorted taxonomies. Eight files are in the EL set and in the development set, so they are two entries and ran twice. t7192.sh ran ore_ont_7192 once per side on one thread in a 14 GiB scope on the laptop, since the 8 GiB scope of the sweep kills both builds on it. The prototype tipb1 fails the unit test a_horn_successor_of_a_real_source_learns_the_source_is_real_in_either_order of the crate, which counts the Real message it removes, so it is kept as a patch and not as a commit.
